# Questions

## Question #1 (1 Point)

Which comparison of test types is MOST accurate in Agile software development?

1. Non-functional testing is performed only after the iteration, while white-box testing is performed only after system testing is complete.

<div></div>

1. Black-box testing is mainly performed before coding begins, while white-box testing is primarily used for regression testing after the iteration.

<div></div>

1. Exploratory testing is typically started after the iteration, while usability testing supplements functional testing activities.

<div></div>

1. Functional testing during the iteration focuses on verifying user story acceptance criteria, while broader functional and integration testing may occur after the iteration.

Select ONE answer.

## Question #2 (1 Point)

Which test types are examples of black-box testing typically performed after the iteration?

1. Usability testing.

<div></div>

1. Security testing.

<div></div>

1. Performance testing.

<div></div>

1. Regression testing.

<div></div>

1. End-to-end testing. Select TWO answers.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Question #3 (1 Point)

Which statements reﬂect the recommended use of end-to-end (E2E) testing in Agile software development?

1. End-to-end (E2E) testing should be the primary test type to ensure completeness

<div></div>

1. A number of critical ﬂows should be veriﬁed during end-to-end (E2E) testing

<div></div>

1. End-to-end (E2E) testing provides fast, detailed diagnostic feedback during coding

<div></div>

1. All regression testing should be performed during end-to-end (E2E) testing for simplicity

<div></div>

1. End-to-end (E2E) testing complements but does not replace testing of the lower areas in the test pyramid

Select TWO answers.

## Question #4 (1 Point)

Assign each of the following pitfalls (1–4) to ONE of the categories (A–B) while not leaving any group empty.

    1. Testing may focus narrowly on predeﬁned test results and delay discovery of critical defects.
    2. Quality evaluation becomes subjective and hard to quantify, making stakeholder trust diﬃcult.
    3. Heavy emphasis on formal work products reduces responsiveness to changes in real system behavior.
    4. Success depends on shared ownership and cultural maturity, which not all software development teams achieve.

<div></div>

    1. Pitfalls mainly associated with formal testing

<div></div>

    1. Pitfalls mainly associated with holistic testing

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Question #5 (1 Point)

Match the regression testing approaches (1–4) with the scenario where they add the MOST value (A–D):

    1. Incremental regression testing
    2. Risk-based regression testing
    3. DevOps-oriented regression testing
    4. Collaborative regression testing

<div></div>

    1. Detecting unintended defects when test automation coverage is incomplete

<div></div>

    1. Ensuring rapid feedback after each code integration

<div></div>

    1. Validating stability of a deployment in pre-production or production with monitoring

<div></div>

    1. Deciding which regression areas need attention after frequent changes to high-risk features

1. 1A, 2C, 3B, 4D

<div></div>

1. 1B, 2D, 3C, 4A

<div></div>

1. 1B, 2A, 3D, 4C

<div></div>

1. 1D, 2B, 3A, 4C Select ONE answer.

## Question #6 (1 Point)

In Agile software development teams, what is the main beneﬁt of combining generalization with specialization?

1. It eliminates the need for experts in specialized areas such as usability or test automation.

<div></div>

1. It enables ﬂexibility across tasks while keeping deep expertise where required.

<div></div>

1. It reduces overlap between roles, ensuring developers and testers stay separate.

<div></div>

1. It preserves strict role boundaries, making ownership of work clearer. Select ONE answer.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Question #7 (1 Point)

Which practices are MOST likely to strengthen a Product Owner’s (PO) motivation to engage in test activities?

1. Providing transparency through dashboards that show quality risks in relation to release readiness.

<div></div>

1. Shifting responsibility for component testing directly to the Product Owner (PO).

<div></div>

1. Handling acceptance criteria solely within the test team to ensure consistency.

<div></div>

1. Involving the Product Owner (PO) in collaborative test execution (e.g. bug bashes).

<div></div>

1. Delegating ownership of regression testing to the Product Owner (PO) without Agile software development team support.

Select TWO answers.

## Question #8 (1 Point)

Which of the following BEST explains how the whole team approach helps developers when working on evolving code?

1. It allows developers to ﬁnalize features before acceptance criteria are discussed

<div></div>

1. It provides continuous testing feedback that enables safe refactoring and quicker corrections

<div></div>

1. It shifts most testing responsibilities to testers so developers can focus solely on coding

<div></div>

1. It prevents business representatives from inﬂuencing technical decisions Select ONE answer.

## Question #9 (1 Point)

Which of the following is BEST shows how the whole team approach assists developers?

1. Developers can start up production-like environments locally or in test.

<div></div>

1. Developers can work independently and in parallel and can experiment safely with code.

<div></div>

1. Developers gain clear, testable acceptance criteria before implementing a user story.

<div></div>

1. Developers know instantly if new code breaks existing behavior. Select ONE answer.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Question #10 (1 Point)

Which situation BEST illustrates an appropriate use of a tissue tester?

1. After a release, asking end users to run acceptance tests in production.

<div></div>

1. Midway through development, running a full usability test session in a usability lab with recruited customers.

<div></div>

1. Early in feature design, brieﬂy showing a colleague from another team to spot usability defects.

<div></div>

1. After ﬁnalizing the infrastructure, running a performance test with performance testers. Select ONE answer.

## Question #11 (1 Point)

Which situations BEST illustrate eﬀective iteration-level test planning in Agile software development?

1. A tester documents all possible test cases for the release before development starts.

<div></div>

1. The team collaborates to reﬁne acceptance criteria during backlog reﬁnement.

<div></div>

1. Developers schedule the test environment setup for the time when unit testing is about to begin.

<div></div>

1. Test automation is prioritized to the extent that manual testing is avoided.

<div></div>

1. The team agrees on which test techniques to apply for the selected user stories. Select TWO answers.

## Question #12 (3 Points)

You are working on a project for a new mobile app. The product is in its early stage and undergoing rapid prototyping due to high change frequency. The delivery approach uses one-week iterations with continuous integration, but features are still evolving based on user feedback. The team concentrates on tests that are business-facing. The product is not yet feature complete, so the focus is on validating ideas and learning quickly rather than fully auditable compliance.

You develop a project test strategy for the next few iterations by mapping test techniques, test types, test levels and test appraoches to test quadrants.

Which potential elements of a project test strategy will be MOST useful in the scenario described above?

1. Perform component testing

<div></div>

1. Perform user acceptance testing (UAT)

<div></div>

1. Perform security testing

<div></div>

1. Perform exploratory testing Select ONE answer.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Question #13 (1 Point)

Which statement BEST describes the diﬀerence between test monitoring in Agile software development and approaches that are considered more sequential?

1. Agile test monitoring focuses on documenting test completion percentages across phases.

<div></div>

1. Agile test monitoring emphasizes continuous visibility through lightweight metrics and trends.

<div></div>

1. Test monitoring in approaches that are considered more sequential relies on real-time dashboards updated throughout the iteration.

<div></div>

1. Monitoring in both approaches uses identical metrics but at diﬀerent project phases. Select ONE answer.

## Question #14 (1 Point)

Which of the following is an example of performing test monitoring in an Agile software development?

1. A burndown chart showing the remaining test eﬀort over time

<div></div>

1. A retrospective resulting with concrete actions to improve test practices

<div></div>

1. An iteration review deciding on adjustments to test scope or priorities

<div></div>

1. Iteration planning deﬁning test objectives and test tasks estimations Select ONE answer.

## Question #15 (1 Point)

Which of the following statements about coverage in Agile test reporting are TRUE?

    1. Code coverage alone is not suﬃcient to demonstrate overall product quality.

<div></div>

    1. Requirements coverage links automated tests to user stories and acceptance criteria.

<div></div>

    1. Exploratory testing coverage can be reported through session-based test management.

<div></div>

    1. Test type coverage ensures that acceptance criteria for individual user stories are veriﬁed.

<div></div>

    1. Infrastructure coverage is calculated by linking automated acceptance tests to user stories.

1. i, ii, and iv

<div></div>

1. i, ii, and iii

<div></div>

1. ii, iii, and v

<div></div>

1. i, iv, and v Select ONE answer.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Question #16 (3 Points)

During the last three iterations, your Agile software development team observed a high cycle time for resolving defects, with defects often lingering in the backlog for multiple days before being addressed. Failure rate and defect detection percentage were observed to be steady at expected levels. The number of ﬂaky tests remains very low. Statement coverage and branch coverage are within acceptable thresholds for critical paths. Automated test pass rates were consistently high. Test environment stability was low due to a few environment-related failures reported.

Which of the following improvement measures is MOST appropriate to address the issue described in the scenario?

1. Strengthen automated testing to increase coverage during component integration testing

<div></div>

1. Refactor tests which are hard to maintain or redundant, using design patterns like page objects

<div></div>

1. Schedule time in each iteration for applying test automation refactoring practices

<div></div>

1. Adopt a whole team approach to defect triage to strengthen collaboration across roles Select ONE answer.

## Question #17 (1 Point)

Match each item (1–4) with the purpose it serves (A–D) when initiating test process improvement in Agile software development.

    1. Test-focused retrospectives
    2. Agile testing self-assessments
    3. Joint risk workshops
    4. Test-ﬁrst approaches (ATDD/BDD)

<div></div>

    1. Establish a baseline and identify gaps in the current test approach

<div></div>

    1. Provide earlier and more actionable feedback in the continuous integration/continuous delivery pipeline

<div></div>

    1. Create shared ownership of quality goals through reﬂection

<div></div>

    1. Align test process improvement eﬀorts with business risks and product risks

1. 1C, 2A, 3B, 4D

<div></div>

1. 1B, 2C, 3D, 4A

<div></div>

1. 1A, 2D, 3C, 4B

<div></div>

1. 1C, 2A, 3D, 4B Select ONE answer.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Question #18 (1 Point)

Assign each of the following testware (1–4) to ONE of the categories (A–B) without leaving any category empty.

    1. Automated acceptance tests
    2. Test charters
    3. Visual models such as process ﬂows or state diagrams
    4. Exploratory test session sheets

<div></div>

    1. Items that provide a clear and stable description of expected behavior

<div></div>

    1. Items that capture insights and understanding that change over time

## Question #19 (1 Point)

Which testware can be used as a form of requirements and, at the same time, documented in a format that allows its automated execution as a test?

1. Examples in behavior-driven development

<div></div>

1. Test charters in session-based exploratory testing

<div></div>

1. Build scripts in continuous delivery

<div></div>

1. Defect reports created during test execution Select ONE answer.

## Question #20 (1 Point)

How can storyboarding and testboarding increase the quality of the test basis?

1. By ensuring that testers do not contribute until coding is complete.

<div></div>

1. By visualizing user journeys to highlight missing steps and risks.

<div></div>

1. By requiring that acceptance criteria remain unchanged throughout iterations.

<div></div>

1. By mapping scenarios in a visible way that improves alignment among roles.

<div></div>

1. By focusing exclusively on regression testing automation. Select TWO answers.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Question #21 (1 Point)

Which of the following BEST describes how example mapping improves the quality of the test basis?

1. By enforcing that every user story has detailed test scripts before coding begins

<div></div>

1. By documenting only functional requirements without addressing hidden assumptions

<div></div>

1. By linking user stories to concrete examples that reduce ambiguity and clarify acceptance criteria

<div></div>

1. By ensuring acceptance criteria are ﬁnalized before reﬁnement sessions begin Select ONE answer.

## Question #22 (1 Point)

Assign each of the following examples (1–4) to ONE of the bias types (A–B) while not leaving any category empty.

    1. A tester only designs tests for the "happy path" and ignores error handling.
    2. Testers continue to focus on the ﬁrst interpretation of a requirement even when new insights arise.
    3. An agile software development team overlooks edge case scenarios because initial user stories were focused on happy paths only.
    4. Testers rely only on verifying expected behaviors, leaving unusual test conditions untested.

<div></div>

    1. Conﬁrmation bias

<div></div>

    1. Anchoring eﬀect

## Question #23 (1 Point)

Which of the following is an example of a CONFIRMATION bias?

    1. The team assumes the initial design of a checkout process is ﬁnal and fails to test alternate payment ﬂows or error handling, resulting in undetected transaction failures

<div></div>

    1. Testers follow the lead of a senior developer who claims a new feature is “low risk,” skipping exploratory testing that could have revealed critical edge-case defects

<div></div>

    1. Testers avoid reporting a recurring performance issue because the majority believes it is "not important," allowing a critical bottleneck to persist into production

<div></div>

    1. A tester only veriﬁes that the login feature works with valid credentials, ignoring attempts with invalid or expired credentials, allowing authentication defects to go undetected

Select ONE answer.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Question #24 (2 Points)

Which of the following statements about applying user story slicing to achieve testable user stories are TRUE?

    1. Splitting a user story into tasks such as “enter data,” “upload document,” and “submit form” is workﬂow slicing that creates testable increments.

<div></div>

    1. Starting with the simplest happy-path example makes the user story immediately veriﬁable and builds a foundation for edge cases later.

<div></div>

    1. Separating backend processing logic from the UI enables testing outputs via APIs before UI workﬂows exist.

<div></div>

    1. Beginning with rare exception cases ensures maximum coverage early in development.

<div></div>

    1. Creating a thin slice that spans database, logic, and UI should be used for every user story to ensure testability.

1. i, ii, and iv

<div></div>

1. i, ii, and iii
